title: Deterministic evidence deltas as world-graph repair guidance
question: Does deterministic Stage-1 evidence improve graph repairs when used alone or alongside the existing validator repair cards without regressing repairs that already work?
hypothesis: A narrowly scoped evidence delta will help restore omitted source facts while existing validator cards continue to repair typed structural faults.

change_under_test.description: Add advisory Stage-1 omission and conditionality findings to repair retries with off, alone, and combined modes.

control.description: Existing typed validator issues, repair cards, deterministic local patches, and transactional repair boundaries.

experimental.description: Evidence delta without existing repair-card prompt
Existing cards plus broad evidence delta
Combined delta excluding shared choice directives
Combined delta omitted from the prompt when it has no actionable findings; regression subset only

held_constant: maximum pairwise audit calls set to zero
world validator and existing repair-card implementation
intentionally_not_compared: causal effect of repair guidance independent of Stage-1 and initial-draft variation
interpretation: Existing typed repair cards materially outperform evidence-only guidance. Broad combined guidance regressed all known-success cases because shared decision directives were misclassified as missing world effects. Excluding shared directives removed that failure family, and suppressing empty deltas reduced prompt perturbation, but the live runs did not establish non-regression or incremental value.

keep: evidence delta builder behind an opt-in flag
exclusion of shared obligations and choice directives
no prompt mutation when the evidence delta is empty
do_not_prioritize: enabling combined evidence guidance by default
decision.next_test: Replay identical frozen Stage-1 inventories and identical rejected candidates through existing-card and combined repair prompts; only include evidence deltas with actionable findings.

limitations: Stage-1 extraction and initial candidate generation were rerun rather than frozen.
The model is not guaranteed bitwise deterministic at temperature zero.
Only four cases were used, with three selected because existing repair guidance had previously succeeded.
The v3 arm used only the three regression cases and is not a complete matched arm.
Some rejected final graphs appeared semantically plausible, indicating validator/admission behavior remains a confound.
